title: Daily arXiv physics | Friday, 6 November 2026 | 8 notable papers
global_caveat: This is an inferred selection, not an official arXiv trending chart; citation history is limited for papers announced yesterday. It is not a readership or download ranking, is not comprehensive coverage, and preprints are not peer-reviewed consensus.

sections.title: Entropic measures of quantum information
sections.abstract: This review surveys quantum information entropies—including Rényi and smooth entropies—their interrelations, and applications in communication, cryptography, resource theories, thermodynamics, and many-body physics.
sections.claimed_result: The authors organize a broad family of quantum-information measures and explain how their mathematical properties connect to operational tasks; this is a review synthesis, not a new physical measurement.
sections.evidence_type: Review; 84-page synthesis of quantum information theory and physics literature.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a literature review, so its conclusions depend on scope and selection of previous work and do not constitute a standalone new physical result.

sections.title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
sections.abstract: The authors compress quantum measurement data into learned overlap models to accelerate hybrid quantum-classical Monte Carlo, reporting chemically accurate calculations up to 40 qubits for hydrogen chains and iron–sulfur clusters using measurements from Google’s Willow processor.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report chemical-accuracy energies at up to 40 qubits and 190-fold and 4,100-fold lower total QC-QMC cost at 8 and 16 qubits, respectively.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; hybrid QMC uses randomized measurements from Google’s Willow processor, with hydrogen-chain and iron–sulfur-cluster benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify overlap-estimation costs that grow sharply with system size; the high-spin iron–sulfur comparison uses classically simulated shadows, rather than a second hardware measurement.

sections.title: Signature of charge-3e tunneling in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
sections.abstract: The authors report an unusual sequence of microwave-induced Shapiro steps in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions whose frequency, power, temperature, and annealing dependences they interpret as an effective charge-3e tunneling process.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret Shapiro steps spaced in units of hf/3e as evidence for a Josephson process involving a trio of electrons in twisted cuprate junctions.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; microwave-driven Shapiro-step and transport measurements on twisted cuprate Josephson junctions, with device and temperature comparisons.
sections.unique_caveat: The microscopic mechanism remains speculative; the authors discuss interlayer excitonic order and note that why the proposed fractional phase term appears without more fundamental terms needs further investigation. The unconventional steps were observed only in two slightly underdoped devices among the reported samples.

sections.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
sections.abstract: The authors construct syndrome-extraction circuits and an online decoder for quantum memories in 2D non-chiral topological orders, and prove a threshold under local stochastic circuit-level noise.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a nonzero threshold for their scheme under local stochastic circuit-level noise and outline logical-gate extensions.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; Turaev–Viro path-integral construction, explicit circuits, decoding algorithm, and mathematical threshold proof.
sections.unique_caveat: This is not a hardware demonstration; the proof assumes the stated noise model and fast, inexpensive classical decoding.

sections.title: Correlations and fluctuations of flow with event shape engineering in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at the LHC
sections.abstract: The ALICE Collaboration measures correlations among flow harmonics in Pb–Pb and Xe–Xe collisions and uses event-shape selection to separate linear and nonlinear contributions to the fourth harmonic.
sections.claimed_result: ALICE reports that the nonlinear component of v4 rises with the selected initial ellipticity while its linear component changes little; the response coefficient is broadly stable except in the most central collisions.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; ALICE measurements of Pb–Pb at 5.02 TeV and Xe–Xe at 5.44 TeV using event-shape engineering and multiparticle correlations.
sections.unique_caveat: Event-shape selection also changes flow-fluctuation estimates and may introduce selection bias; the v3–v4 anticorrelation is not statistically significant, and the central-collision response differs from the broader trend.

sections.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
sections.abstract: The authors derive and simulate the cross-covariance between two fast-radio-burst dispersion-measure observables, then forecast how combining them with LSST-like weak lensing can constrain cosmic baryons and host contributions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that the cross-covariance has little impact on wide-area constraints in their setup, while adding the Macquart relation to an LSST-like lensing forecast tightens the physical baryon-density constraint by 32% and the mean host contribution by a factor of 4.1.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; halo-model covariance derivation, log-normal FRB forward simulations, and an LSST-like weak-lensing forecast.
sections.unique_caveat: Forecasts depend on the halo and electron-distribution models and assumed survey; the authors show that a 20% error in the mean DM–redshift relation can bias the inferred DM power by up to 2σ per band in a large-catalogue scenario.

sections.title: The cold substellar frontier in JWST Extragalactic surveys: a robust parallax measurement yields the most distant known ultra-cold Y dwarf
sections.abstract: Using multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam astrometry, the authors measure a parallax for a very cold Y dwarf in the JADES field, placing it about three times farther away than previously parallax-measured Y dwarfs and estimating its luminosity and likely planetary-mass regime.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer a distance of 64 pc with asymmetric uncertainty of +6/−5 pc and bolometric luminosity log(Lbol/Lsun) = −7.08 ± 0.09; evolutionary models place the object in the planetary-mass regime.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam imaging, astrometric calibration, and near-infrared spectral analysis.
sections.unique_caveat: The planetary-mass interpretation depends on evolutionary and atmospheric models; the paper says current atmospheric models do not reproduce the spectral energy distribution in detail.

sections.title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
sections.abstract: The authors use lattice-QCD spectra at two pion masses, combined with chiral effective-field-theory analyses, to estimate how deuteron and dineutron scattering properties vary with quark mass.
sections.claimed_result: Both EFT schemes indicate that the deuteron becomes unbound near a pion mass of 220 MeV; this is an extrapolated estimate, not a direct calculation at that precise mass.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; lattice-QCD finite-volume spectra at pion masses around 200 and 280 MeV, supplemented by chiral EFT and comparison with physical-point phenomenology and an earlier heavier-mass calculation.
sections.unique_caveat: The unbinding point is inferred from a limited set of pion masses and EFT extrapolations, so its location depends on truncation and input assumptions.
